**D2 PR3 — reverter-skip gap: must gate candidate M on independent offender status**

**What**: While implementing D2 PR3's reverter-skip wiring in `brain-audit.mjs`, discovered that an unrestricted reverter-skip search (candidate M = "any merge in the window") lets a NEW, illegitimate offender (a later merge re-adding a previously-reverted payload — design §7.1 A5) get wrongly exempted by matching a clean, non-offending, LEGITIMATE revert merge R as its "M" — because `isReverterOf`/`isResolvedAt` are pure tree-effect symmetry checks and don't know which side is "the offender". Fixed by adding an `isOffender(m.sha)` gate (`isRawOffender` in brain-audit.mjs) that independently verifies the matched M actually fails >=1 of the 4 governance checks on its own diff (commit-body-only, no PR-metadata fetch — documented simplification, false-positive-safe direction) BEFORE accepting the reverter-skip.

**Why**: Design §3.3 states the reverter-skip fires "iff there exists a merge M ... such that isReverterOf(M,R)" without explicitly restricting M to genuine offenders — but the narrative context (R is "the auto-revert of a FLAGGED offender") requires it. Caught via TDD: my own A5 E2E test (re-introduction after revert) failed because "later" (re-adding SECRET_PAYLOAD) was byte-identical, read backward, to R's own forward contribution (R removed that payload) — so `isReverterOf(R, later)` was true, and without the offender gate, "later" got silently `[SKIP] revert of R` instead of staying `[FAIL]`. A naive fix (restrict M candidates to `resolved-skip`-matched shas, tracked oldest-first) was ALSO insufficient — it turned out `isResolvedAt(R, HEAD)` ITSELF returns true for R (since "later" is R's exact tree-inverse too), so R got added to the tracking set and the bug reappeared one level deeper. The robust fix required independently re-verifying M's own violation status, not relying on any resolved-skip bookkeeping.

**Where**: `brain/scripts/brain-audit.mjs` — `reverterSkipLine(candidate, merges, {git, isOffender})`, new `isRawOffender(sha, {cwd, ignoreList, allObservations})` helper, call site inside the per-merge loop's failure branch.

**Learned**: Pure tree-effect symmetry predicates (`normDiff` equality) cannot distinguish "M is the offender, R reverted it" from "R is a clean action, X coincidentally undid R" — they only prove an exact inverse relationship exists. Any wiring that uses such a predicate to grant an exemption MUST independently confirm which side deserves the exemption (here: M must be a genuine check-failure on its own diff) rather than trusting resolved-skip's own coincidental match as proof of "M was an offender". This is a generalizable lesson for any future reverter/skip mechanism built on `resolution.mjs`'s primitives.
